To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) students in multilingual classrooms code-switch when providing explanations to virtual peers in a learning system, (2) students code-switch to improve the quality of their explanations, (3) students code-switch when their explanations are not well received by the virtual peer, and (4) the quality of explanations and affective valences are not significantly different when students code-switch.
code-switching is prevalent in multilingual classrooms, and that students' use of code-switching can be explained by cognitive and social motivations.
students use code-switching in a personalized learning environment to communicate with the pedagogical agent, with other students, and with themselves.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and evaluation of learning systems in a multilingual context.
how students use a learning technology to learn mathematics, with a focus on the role of code-switching.
how students use code-switching to explain mathematical problem solving in a virtual peer system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
code switching is a natural phenomenon in multilingual environments and it is important to consider it when designing educational technology.

students used code-switched speech to explain algebra problem solving in a personalized learning system, and that the quality of their explanations was related to their affective valence, which in turn was related to code-switching motivations.
the use of code-switching is an important part of learning interactions with a pedagogical agent, and that the agent should be designed to support multilingual learners.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the design of personalized learning systems must account for the multilingual nature of many classrooms.
students in multilingual settings use code-switching to help them learn, and we should be more sensitive to this when designing technology for learning.
code-switching is a complex phenomenon that has both positive and negative effects on learning and social dynamics in a classroom.
The main takeaway from our work is that
code-switching is a powerful tool to help students learn and that learning systems need to account for it.
the design of learning by teaching systems should be informed by the multilingual context in which they are used.
we can design systems to support code-switching, and in so doing, support multilingual students.
